title: The Best Damn Pan-Seared Pork Chops

source.name: Best Damn Pan Seared Pork Chops - Recipe Teacher

steps: Pat pork chops dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add pork chops and sear for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until a golden-brown crust develops.
Flip chops, add butter to pan, and sear for another 3 to 4 minutes on second side.
Hold chops upright with tongs for 30 seconds to render and crisp the outer fat cap.
Remove chops when internal temperature reaches 145°F. Spoon pan juices over meat and let rest for 3 to 5 minutes before serving.
swaps: Boneless pork chops can be used (cook 1 minute less per side); brown sugar can be added to the rub.
notes: Cast-iron skillet creates the golden crust while keeping the interior juicy and tender.

title: Juicy Skillet Pork Chops with Pan Sauce

source.name: The Best Juicy Skillet Pork Chops Recipe - Inspired Taste

steps: Pat chops dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chops and sear until golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip chops. Hold upright with tongs for 30 seconds to sizzle the fat cap.
Reduce heat to low, cover skillet with lid, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until internal temperature reads 145°F.
Transfer chops to a warm plate and rest.
In the same skillet over medium heat, add garlic, butter, broth, apple cider vinegar, and fresh herbs, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Pour pan sauce over chops and serve.
swaps: Can use boneless chops; apple juice can replace wine for a sweeter profile.
notes: Covering the skillet on low heat locks in moisture and cooks chops evenly without drying them out.

title: Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder with Crispy Crackling

source.name: Pork Roast with Crispy Crackling - RecipeTin Eats

ingredients.name: onions, halved (to elevate meat in pan)

steps: Use a sharp utility knife to score the rind in thin parallel lines 1/3 inch apart (cut through skin into fat, but not into meat).
Pour boiling water over the skin to open cuts, then pat completely dry with paper towels.
Rub oil and fennel seeds on flesh side only. Rub coarse salt generously all over scored skin, pressing deep into grooves.
Place halved onions in a roasting pan and set pork on top so skin is level.
Roast at 320°F (160°C) for 2.5 hours until flesh is tender and juicy.
Turn oven to 485°F (250°C) and blast pork for 25 to 30 minutes until skin puffs, bubbles, and turns into shatter-crisp crackling.
Rest loosely tented with foil for 15 to 20 minutes before carving into succulent slices with crackling.
swaps: Pork belly can be used with the identical method and timing.
notes: The ultimate crackling technique: low slow roast for tender flesh, followed by maximum heat blast.

title: Easy Slow-Cooker BBQ Pulled Pork

source.name: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork (Easy Recipe) - Fifteen Spatulas

ingredients.name: garlic powder, onion powder, and cumin

steps: In a small bowl, mix brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, salt, and pepper into a rub.
Rub seasoning blend all over pork shoulder.
Place sliced onions in the bottom of a slow cooker or Dutch oven. Pour in apple cider vinegar.
Set pork shoulder on top of onions. Cover and cook on low heat for 6 hours (or 3 hours in 325°F Dutch oven) until fork-tender (200°F internal).
Transfer pork to a large cutting board and shred with two forks, discarding any large fat deposits.
Return shredded pork to cooker juices, stir in barbecue sauce, and pile high on toasted brioche buns.
swaps: Can serve over baked potatoes, sweet potatoes, or nachos instead of buns.
notes: Tossing shredded meat back into braising juices ensures it stays moist and flavorful.

title: Southwest-Spiced Roast Pork Tenderloin

source.name: Know Your Pork Cuts - National Pork Board

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C) and line a shallow roasting pan with foil.
Trim silvery connective tissue from tenderloin. Rub with olive oil.
Combine chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper; rub spice blend over all sides of tenderloin.
Roast in preheated oven for 18 to 20 minutes until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part reads 145°F.
Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes tented with foil.
Slice against the grain into thick medallions and serve with black beans, corn, or roasted peppers.
swaps: Can serve with salsa verde, chimichurri, or mango salsa.
notes: Lean tenderloin cooks quickly; removing at 145°F keeps meat wonderfully juicy and pink.

title: Oven-Roasted Juicy Pork Tenderloin (Skills Showdown Winner)

source.name: We Tested 7 Methods for Cooking Juicy Pork Tenderloin | The Kitchn

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C). Trim silverskin from tenderloin and pat dry.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear tenderloin for 2 minutes per side (6 to 8 minutes total) until golden-brown on all sides.
In a small bowl, mix Dijon mustard, maple syrup, minced garlic, and rosemary.
Brush maple-mustard glaze over seared tenderloin.
Transfer skillet directly into oven and roast for 10 to 12 minutes until internal temperature hits 145°F.
Rest for 5 to 10 minutes before slicing into medallions.
swaps: Can use whole grain mustard; honey can substitute for maple syrup.
notes: Voted #1 method across 7 tested techniques for delivering the juiciest, most flavorful tenderloin.

title: Oven-Baked St. Louis Style BBQ Ribs

source.name: The Ultimate Guide to Pork Ribs - Smithfield

steps: Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Flip ribs bone-side up and use a butter knife and paper towel to grip and peel off the papery membrane.
Combine brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt, and pepper; rub over both sides of ribs.
Wrap the seasoned rack tightly in heavy-duty aluminum foil, crimping edges to seal in steam, and place on a baking sheet.
Bake in oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until meat is tender and has pulled back 1/4 inch from bone tips.
Carefully unwrap foil and brush meat generously with barbecue sauce.
Return to oven under broiler or at 425°F for 5 to 10 minutes until barbecue sauce bubbles and caramelizes into a sticky glaze.
Rest 10 minutes, slice between bones, and serve.
swaps: Baby back ribs can be used (bake 2 to 2.5 hours); homemade or bottled barbecue sauce works.
notes: Tender fall-off-the-bone ribs achieved in home ovens without a smoker.

title: Slow-Roasted Pork Belly with Blistered Crackling Skin

source.name: The Temperature Trick For Crispy Skin On Slow-Roasted Pork Belly - Tasting Table

ingredients.name: Chinese five-spice powder or fennel powder

steps: Score pork skin with sharp knife into shallow diamond cross-hatching without cutting into meat.
Pour boiling water over skin, dry thoroughly, brush skin with vinegar, and chill uncovered in refrigerator overnight.
Rub five-spice powder, white pepper, garlic powder, and salt into meat side only. Rub coarse salt generously into skin.
Preheat oven to 325°F (163°C). Place belly on a wire rack inside a roasting pan.
Roast for 2 hours until pork is tender and fat has rendered.
Crank oven heat to 450°F (232°C) and roast for 20 to 30 minutes until skin blisters, bubbles, and turns into crispy golden crackling.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing with a serrated knife.
swaps: Can use Italian herbs (rosemary/garlic) instead of five-spice for porchetta style.
notes: The high-heat blast renders out fat and turns the rind into delicate shatter-crisp crackling.

title: Oven-Baked Bone-In Pork Loin Chops

source.name: How to Cook Pork Chops: Juicy Every Time (Oven, Grill & Pan) - Cookpad

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Brush bone-in chops on both sides with olive oil.
In a small dish, mix paprika, garlic powder, thyme, salt, and pepper; rub seasoning over all chops.
Arrange chops on baking sheet with space between them.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until internal temperature registers 145°F on a digital meat thermometer.
Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving with roasted vegetables or mashed potatoes.
swaps: Can bread chops with seasoned breadcrumbs or parmesan before baking.
notes: Hands-off weeknight baking method that retains moisture when cooked accurately to 145°F.
